enAudit: NEW — G1-282: the instruction reads "The capital letter and the end mark show where each sentence begins." The end mark shows where the sentence ENDS. This is a different defect from the already-fixed full-stop/end-mark wording: the sentence as written tells the child both clues mark the START, which makes the end mark useless as a clue. (Swedish ships the corrected split: capital = start, mark = end.)

NEW — G1-268: the instruction is "A bottom brick is missing. Use the brick above to find it." On the render only ONE bottom brick is missing but every brick in the three rows above is also empty, so the child must build the whole wall — which the instruction never asks for. Its siblings G1-266 and G1-267 both say "to the top". Suggest: "A bottom brick is missing. Work it out, then build the wall to the top."

NEW — G1-270: the instruction is "Double the group, then halve it." No card asks for both. Each card carries a single chip reading either "double" or "half" (the render is 2 doubles + 2 halves), so nothing on the page is doubled and then halved. Suggest: "Double the group on some cards and halve it on others."

NEW — G1-252: card 2 reads "Make 4 ufos purple." The acronym is lowercased; it should be "UFOs". Same page, card 6 uses the Latin plural "cacti" in a Grade-1 read-and-do sentence where "cactuses" is the register a 6-7 year old decodes.

NEW — G1-251 and G1-252: the sentence frames mix declaratives with imperatives on one page. "Tom colors 2 giraffes blue." (G1-251 card 1) and "Max colors 3 helicopters blue." (G1-252 card 3) sit beside "Color 3 parrots red." and "Find 2 roosters and color them green." A declarative about a third party is not an instruction the child can act on unless they infer they are Tom. Every card on a read-and-do page should be addressed to the reader.

NEW — G2-297: the title "A Busy Month" and the instruction "This month is full." both promise a fuller calendar than the render shows. What actually differs from G2-296 is the number of QUESTIONS (six vs four); the calendar itself carries one extra picture event (three vs two), which no child would read as "full". The honest distinguishing element is the question count, and that is what the Swedish title ships.

NEW — K-296: unlike its siblings K-294 and K-295, the instruction never mentions the orange start dot, although the render draws one at 11 exactly as they do. A child who has just done K-294/K-295 is told where to begin and here is not.

NEW — G2-299: the instruction claims "The word bank names everything." The bank names every distinct KIND in the scene (four), but the scene draws five animals because the raccoon appears twice. For a child who counts objects rather than kinds the claim is false. Suggest "The word bank names each animal you see."

SHARPENS the known G3 grouping item — the defect is the WRAP, and it can display the wrong answer. G3-375 card 2 says "Lily arranges 20 koalas in rows of 5. How many rows does Lily make?" and the picture wraps the 20 objects into 2 visible rows of 10. The answer is 4, the picture shows 2. Same wrap on G3-374 card 2 (10 objects in one row of 10, story says rows of 5), G3-376 card 1 ("3 rows of legos" drawn as 3 boxes side by side in ONE row) and G3-376 card 3. Wrapping the pile to a multiple of the stated group size would fix all of them.

CORROBORATES the known G1-264 item, with the count: the page shows six words in TWO pairs (baby/boat, scooter/swing) while the instruction says "Two words start alike." Four words do. The Swedish ships "Two pairs start alike".

CORROBORATES the known G2-293 duplicate: on the three-card render, card 1 and card 3 are the SAME problem — both buy the 40-unit fish, both pay with two 25 coins, both are Mia. All three cards also pay with the identical 25+25, so nothing on the page varies the coin reading.

CORROBORATES the known G2-281 names gap: the render carries "anna has a big fox" and "ben likes the little donkey", but the key strip lists only "Capital letter" and "End mark" — the "Names" chip that was added to G2-282 is missing here, so the proper nouns are silently required and never cued.

LOCALE-CONFIG (sv, not the English source): the Swedish meta description reads "Gratis utskrivbart arbetsblad: {TITLE} Arbetsblad (Frukter) för Förskoleklass." — the word arbetsblad appears twice, because seo.words.free_printable in frontend/messages/sv.json is "Gratis utskrivbart arbetsblad:" while the engine appends worksheet="Arbetsblad" after the title. Every Swedish deck description in the catalog carries the duplication. The fix is to set free_printable to "Gratis utskrivbart" (or drop the appended word for sv); it is outside this draft and affects far more than these 64 faces.

NEW — G1-292 SILENTLY SHIPS THE WRONG THEME, and it is the exact defect gen-b2var-waves.js says pinning was written to eliminate. The wave pins every locale to `toys`, but K-288's gender-mix guard needs two distinct article keys and neither sv nor en has a second one in that theme (measured over the countable pool: sv toys 24 en-words / 0 ett; en toys 22 'a' / 0 'an'; for comparison sv fruits 18/2). The build throws, the generator's theme-retry swallows it, and the staged ZIPs prove the substitution already happened: 9 locales shipped wsg-...-g1292-toys-..., but sv shipped -fruits- and en shipped -animals-, while both wave files still read toys. The deck slug and every landing sentence written from the wave map will name a theme the page does not show. Fix: add 'G1-292':'fruits' to EXCEPT.sv (it already carries K-306/K-307 for this reason), choose a second theme for en, and make the retry FAIL LOUD on a pinned themeOverride instead of substituting. (da/no toys each carry exactly one et-noun, so they pass on a coin-flip rather than by design.)

NEW — G1-292 sort bins hold 5 ruled lines but the page issues 8 word chips, and the mix guard only floors each column at 1 (it relaxes to 1 after 200 attempts), so a legal split is 7/1. The measured sv/fruits render is 6 en-words against 5 lines — a child is asked to write six words on five lines on the very first build. Either the bin needs cards-1 lines or the card count needs to be 2x the line count.

NEW — G1-293 'Two bins with pictures' is wrong twice over, and the second one is a pedagogical leak. The bins carry no pictures (they carry an icon-in-a-circle heading and the labels Substantiv/Verb); the pictures sit on the word CHIPS — and only on the noun chips, because the picture comes from the vocab entry. So on the render 'bil, spade, kritor, lego, robot' each show a picture and 'hoppa, springa, sjunga, sova, sitta' show none. The child can sort the whole page correctly by 'has a picture' without reading a word, which is the opposite of what a word-class sort is for.

NEW — G1-298/G1-299 'No pictures to count' denies the one thing on the card that looks countable. With numeric:true the stage is dotPanel(), a white box printed with an even grid of faint dots (the render shows two rows of ten). It is a jotting workspace (data-lcs-workspace) and the English never mentions it, so a child told there is nothing to count sees twenty dots and is given no use for them. Name the workspace instead of denying the pictures.

NEW — G2-311 promises per CARD what the page delivers only once. needQ:1 requires at least ONE question anywhere on the page, but the title 'Two Sentences: Full Stop or Question Mark?' and the instruction 'Two sentences ran together, and one of them is a question' are read as a claim about each card. On the sv render card 3 is 'vera ser tre mangos mina mangos ar jattefina' — two statements, no question at all. (Swedish ships 'Ibland ar en av meningarna ocksa en fraga.')

NEW — G2-312 'How Many Days Later?' names one of its four questions. The question set is stickerDate / after / weekLater / dayOfDate: only `after` asks how many days later. The instruction 'Use the calendar to work out each date' is wrong for two more of them — `after` wants a NUMBER OF DAYS and `dayOfDate` wants a WEEKDAY, and neither is a date. Both title and instruction describe a quarter of the page.

NEW — K-308 repeats the K-296 defect the last panel found, and here it costs more. The instruction never mentions the orange start dot although the render draws one, exactly as K-294/K-295 do — but on this face the orange dot sits on 10, not on 1, so it is the only thing telling the child that the highest number is the starting point. A child who has just done K-294 will start at 1 and draw the figure inside out.

NEW — K-315 'Copy the Capitals' names the wrong unit and reads as capital cities. The child copies a WORD (TARNING, KRITOR, LEGO) that happens to be set in capitals, twice, from a caption model. 'Look at the capitals, then write them yourself' also drops the 'twice' that its sibling K-311 states for the identical two-rail layout — the two faces describe the same scaffold with different amounts of information.

NEW — G2-308 'Write each square in the list for its color' is not grammatical English and hides the task. The child reads a filled picture and writes the code of every square of one colour into that colour's list. Suggest: 'The picture is already coloured in. Write the code of each square in its colour's list.'

NEW — K-310 'Trace each word in big capital letters' describes only the middle lane. The row is a SOLID model, then a dashed lane, then one empty lane, so the child reads, traces and then writes once; 'big' carries nothing that CAPITAL does not.

LOCALE-DATA (sv, not the English source; §10.3 so flagged not fixed) — image-vocabulary.js gives mango the Swedish plural 'mangos', which is an anglicism; SAOL has mango/mangon/mangor. It reaches the child on K-313 (the solid given word) and inside the G1-302 and G2-311 sentence banks, i.e. printed as the model to copy. 'kiwier' and 'papayor' on the same page are correct.

CORROBORATES the LOCALE-CONFIG item already in this draft — the doubled worksheet word is now measurable on all 36 new faces: every sv description reads 'Gratis utskrivbart arbetsblad: <title> Arbetsblad (<tema>) for <arskurs>.' seo.words.free_printable in frontend/messages/sv.json should be 'Gratis utskrivbart'.
